title: Prefill/Decode Scheduler Autotuner and Golden Trajectory
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Problem: tail-latency variance across mixed-prefill workloads is a recurring source of regressions in CI and production. Existing bench suites capture average throughput but miss deterministic sources of jitter (kernel switching, cold KV caches, attention-window spikes).

Goal: build an autotuner-driven scheduler and a reproducible 'golden trajectory' seeding methodology that: (1) identifies stable kernel routing hysteresis points for a given workload mix, (2) tunes prefill chunking and decode pacing to minimize p99 latency while preserving throughput, and (3) produces a deterministic golden baseline artifact we can pin in CI perf gates.

Scope: implement scheduler autotuner service that runs mixed-prefill synthetic workloads, measures per-kernel latency distributions and attention-sparsity effects, and outputs recommended scheduler knobs (batch size, prefill window, kernel-route penalty, KV-warm threshold). Integrate golden-trajectory generation into bench harness so CI can run a reproducible canonical run and detect regressions against pinned baselines.
activities: 2025-06-13: Kickoff meeting with serving-runtime, bench-team, and SRE. Agreed success metrics: <=5% throughput loss for p99 latency reduction >=20% on mixed chat+completion traffic.

2025-06-15: POC autotuner implemented (bayesian optimizer over batch_size, prefill_chunk_tokens, route_penalty). Ran 50 experiments on small GPUs (A100-40GB) using mixed-prefill corpus (short, long, embedded-code). Observed p99 improvement median 18%, with tail variance reduced by 32% for one-shot kernels.

2025-06-17: Discovered regressions when route_penalty > 0.6 for sparse-attention sequences — increased decode stalls due to excessive kernel stickiness. Decision: add hysteresis window and per-workload safelist to avoid over-tuning for pathological sparsity patterns.
2025-06-19: Implemented deterministic warm-prefix seeding: prefix KV warming using canonical tokenized traces to reduce cold-KV variance. Bench run shows 9% p99 reduction on short-chat-heavy mixes.

2025-06-21: Integration branch opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8242. Bench harness changes live in bench/trajectory-runner. Perf dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/inference/boards/trajectory-562431 (internal).

2025-06-23: Design review with PM and Console teams. PM requested explicit rollout plan: (a) feature flag + canary on dedicated pools, (b) telemetry hooks for kernel-choice flips, (c) auto-rollback on latency regressions. Added to acceptance criteria.

2025-06-24: Running extended golden-run: 200-shot deterministic seed across 3 model variants (7B, 13B quantized, 70B). Found a 3% throughput regression on 70B quantized when prefill_chunk_tokens increased beyond 1024. Root cause: kernel memory fragmentation in batched KV allocation. Filed low-priority follow-up: ENG-562612.

2025-06-25: CI integration prototype pushed: bench harness exposes baseline artifact (trajectory.json) and comparator that computes p50/p95/p99 diffs and a kernel-flip histogram. Next: stabilize artifact format and add to runtime-1.19 perf gates.
acceptance_criteria: Autotuner produces stable knob recommendations for at least 3 canonical workload mixes (chat-heavy, long-completion, mixed code) with reproducible improvement in p99 >= 15% vs current baseline.
Golden trajectory artifact format defined and committed; CI comparator can run in <30m and emit p50/p95/p99 diffs + kernel-flip histogram.
Feature-flagged rollout plan documented with canary steps; telemetry hooks added for kernel route flips and prefill chunk counters.
No customer-facing throughput regressions >5% observed in dedicated canary pools for pinned workloads after autotuner knobs applied.
Bench harness and autotuner unit/integration tests added; PR reviewed and approved by runtime and bench leads.
notes: Trade-offs: more aggressive route_penalty reduces kernel thrashing but increases chance of sticky suboptimal kernels — mitigated via hysteresis and safelists.
We opted for bayesian optimizer for sample efficiency; next step is to evaluate bandit-style online tuning for production adaptation.
Deterministic seeding increases CI runtime (extra warm-prefix runs) but yields much lower false positive rate for perf gates; plan to amortize cost by running golden compare only on release branches.
Follow-ups: ENG-562612 (kernel fragmentation investigation), ENG-562790 (console telemetry visualization for kernel flips).
